Personally, I'm against this change. One of the main problems we had with Reddit was that it was incredibly confusing to get into. I'm pretty tech-savvy, but personally for me it took occasional visits over a long period of time before I became familiar with exactly how to navigate and effectively use the site. One of the things I had no trouble understanding though were moderators. Most people know what the term means, it's familiar. I like the fact that we're crafting a culture and creating out own terms for things like the subverses, the upvoats/goats and earlier I saw someone refer to the site as the play pen, however regardless of if these terms were called subreddits or subverses, someone wouldn't understand them at first and would gradually come to understand their use. Compare that to moderator, which they would instantly understand the purpose of initially. If we change it to Shepherd or Goatherd, we've suddenly change this situation into a phrase that will not immediately be understood and must be learned over time. This makes the site more difficult to use and less engaging for newer users.

That's my thoughts on the matter, what do y'all think?

Maybe you would understand it, but also understand you're looking at this from a perspective of a 2 month old user + potentially extensive experience on a site that is practically identical to this one. Change your perspecitve for a second. A 50 year old technophobe goes to Voat because his grandson raved about it. He's never used Reddit before and he's never used Voat before. He sees the term subverse. He doesn't understand it. He sees the term Upvoat, he vaguely understands its meaning but not it's purpose. Now let's look at two scenarios. He sees the term Moderator. Oh, I know what that is. Someone who moderates things! Huzzah, success. I'm learning. Or, he sees the term herder. Now he's really confused and thinks his grandson is into some weird shit. Am I saying that over time he would not be able to come to understand these terms? No, certainly not. Eventually, he would understand it however many technophobes are intimidated by the internet and recognizing a term and understanding it can be the small happiness that makes them stick around for a bit longer and feel more confident.

The crux of what I'm saying is, Voat is small enough already and it's not growing very fast outside of migration periods. Do we want to stifle this growth even further for a relatively minor change? A possible solution however, is to allow subverse moderators to change what their title is called. I wouldn't suggest that one, as it will become a clusterfuck of different titles. Another option is to make it a preference. Default to moderator, allow it to be changed to herder. There's also downsides to that, for example, creating a divide between newer users who see herder being mentioned (maybe auto correct it to moderator according to preferences?) and not understanding it.

Personally, I don't think it's that big a deal, just something that could help Voat a little. And every little helps. Would changing the term moderators to herders kill the site? Nah. But it would dissuade some users. A very small amount mind you, but once again every little helps. I'd like to note I'm just expressing my opinion and mean no offense to you what so ever! D:
